claim.pdf_says: (operand-1<sub>1</sub> + operand-1<sub>2</sub> + ... + operand-1<sub>n</sub> + operand-2)  [general rule 2; subscripts printed as subscripts]
claim.why_it_matters: Same subscript flattening as in general rule 1: 'operand-11' and 'operand-12' read as different operand names instead of operand-1 subscript 1 and subscript 2.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered PDF page 491 (printed page 467), 14.9.2.3 ADD statement general rule 2, shows the expression '(operand-1 + operand-1 + ... + operand-1 + operand-2)' with the 1, 2 and n set as typographic subscripts after each 'operand-1'. page-491.md line 29 reads '(operand-11 + operand-12 + ... + operand-1n + operand-2)': the subscripts are flattened inline, so the transcription names the metavariables operand-11, operand-12 and operand-1n instead of the 1st, 2nd and nth instance of operand-1. Both sources are quoted accurately. Formatting alone does not explain this: the subscript carries the meaning, and the flattened text reads as different operand names. The following sentence ('the values of operand-1 are ...') lets a careful reader recover the intent, but the transcribed expression itself is wrong. The same defect occurs in general rule 1 (md line 17), which the claim notes.
